reason: Attaching algae to stone seems a promising start toward an underwater forest.
expectation: I expect rooted or attached algae, perhaps a step toward a kelp forest.

alternatives.reason: Shore animals could help populate the coast, but I want to pursue the forest first.

effect: The algae and rock made a kelp forest and revealed a new cave goal. Ocean and air may be a route to waves.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the forest become shelter for other organisms.
reason: Combining ocean and air seems like a practical way to make waves for the cave goal.
expectation: I expect wind-driven waves, though the result could be something else.

alternatives.reason: Swimming animals might use the new forest, but I want to pursue the newly revealed goal.

effect: Ocean and air made waves, which can now be combined with stone for the cave goal.
reaction: The result was predictable and useful.
reason: Waves acting on stone seem the direct route to hollowing a cave.
expectation: I expect wave erosion to create a sea cave.

effect: Waves hollowed a sea cave, completing that goal; the coast still needs life.
reaction: The explanation of waves exploiting cracks made the predictable result more concrete.
reason: Soft-bodied animals on the tidal shore seem a direct way to populate the coast.
expectation: I expect a shore habitat or community of animals.

alternatives.reason: Swimming animals could populate the kelp forest, but the shore seems closer to the remaining goal.

effect: The shore combination created coral, suggesting a route toward a coastal community.
reaction: The reminder that stationary coral polyps are animals was interesting.
reason: Coral and algae may form a partnership that supports a reef and its inhabitants.
expectation: I expect a coral-algae partnership, perhaps leading to a reef.

alternatives.reason: Animals in the kelp forest might also build a community, but coral seems promising for the coast goal.

effect: Coral and algae formed a reef partnership, suggesting minerals may help build the reef.
reaction: The mutual exchange and its vulnerability to stress were interesting.
reason: The reef partnership and mineral-rich sea seem the most direct route toward a crowded coastal reef.
expectation: I expect a reef structure to form, though I am unsure how the minerals will be used.

alternatives.reason: Swimming animals could populate the kelp forest, but I want to follow the coral partnership first.

effect: The partnership and dissolved minerals built a coral reef, but the coastal-life goal remains open.
reaction: The idea of successive skeletons creating inherited architecture was interesting.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may bring animals into a habitat.
expectation: I expect swimming animals to inhabit the kelp forest, though I am unsure whether that will complete the coast goal.

effect: The kelp forest shelters young swimmers, creating nursery waters that can now be combined with the reef.
reaction: The connection between habitat and juvenile survival was satisfying.
reason: This is the only offered combination and seems likely to bring the coastal habitats together.
expectation: I expect a diverse coastal community, perhaps completing the remaining goal.

effect: The nursery waters and reef created a coastal mosaic, but the coast goal remains open; tides are the only offered combination.
reaction: The distinction between cooler kelp beds and warmer reefs made the combined habitat more credible.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may connect the coastal habitats through tidal movement.
expectation: I expect tides to enrich or connect the coastal community, perhaps completing the goal.
